skill.name: priority-judge
skill.description: A task prioritization assistant that turns a messy task list into a focused plan using clarity, deadlines, and next actions.
skill.summary: Ranks tasks by clarity and deadline so users know what to do now.
skill.author: yunshu0909

security_audit.summary: All external command static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or inline code formatting in SKILL.md. The high-entropy heuristic is also a false positive because the file is readable Markdown with Chinese text, emoji, and table formatting, not binary or encrypted content. One low semantic issue remains: the skill instructs the assistant to create and save a Markdown priority document, so file writes should require user confirmation.

remediation.issue: User-directed file creation can modify the workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit confirmation before creating files, show the target path, and avoid overwriting existing files without consent.

content.value_statement: Many task lists are hard to act on because deadlines and task clarity are mixed together. This skill asks focused questions and returns a short priority plan for immediate action.
actual_capabilities: Collects unordered tasks from the user through conversation.
Asks whether each task is clear, urgent, and specific.
Ranks tasks using clarity and deadline as the main criteria.
Highlights one or two tasks that should be handled first.
Creates a simple Markdown priority list when requested.
limitations: It depends on accurate user-provided deadlines and task details.
It does not replace a full project management system.
It is not designed for detailed time-blocking or minute-level schedules.
File creation should be confirmed before saving any Markdown document.

use_cases.title: Choose Today's Focus
use_cases.description: Turn a long personal task list into one or two actions for today.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Weekly Work Plan
use_cases.description: Sort work items by deadline and clarity before starting the week.

use_cases.title: Unblock Creative Work
use_cases.description: Separate clear creative tasks from unclear ideas that need more thinking.

prompt_templates.title: Sort My Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: I have many things to do. Help me decide what to do first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My Day
prompt_templates.prompt: Here are my tasks for today: [tasks]. Ask me what you need, then choose the top priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Rank a Work Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backlog and rank it by clarity, deadline, and action value: [backlog].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Priority Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build a Markdown priority plan for this week. Include must-do tasks, optional tasks, delayed tasks, and reasons.

output_examples.input: I need to write a report, call a client, clean notes, and think about a new project.
output_examples.output: Top priority: call the client if there is a deadline today. Next: write the report if the structure is clear. Delay the new project until the goal is clearer.

output_examples.input: I have ten ideas and no clear order.
output: Must do now: items with clear next steps and real deadlines.
Do later: clear items without deadlines.
Clarify first: ideas that still lack a concrete next action.

best_practices: Provide deadlines, task context, and current blockers for each item.
Use the recommendation to choose one or two immediate actions.
Review and adjust the plan when deadlines or task clarity changes.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a complete project management database.
Do not ask for a priority decision without sharing deadline details.
Do not save files unless the target path and overwrite behavior are clear.

faq.question: What does this skill optimize for?
faq.answer: It optimizes for immediate focus by comparing task clarity and deadlines.

faq.question: Can it manage complex projects?
faq.answer: It can help triage priorities, but it does not replace project management software.

faq.question: Does it create task files?
faq.answer: It can produce a Markdown priority list when requested and confirmed.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: It is useful for people with many tasks and unclear starting points.

faq.question: Does it need private data?
faq.answer: No. Share only the task details and deadlines needed for prioritization.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Claude Code, and Codex.
